source_row.rationale: Benchmarking compares an organization's performance measures or practices with external standards or peer organizations to identify improvement opportunities, so Option A is correct. Surveillance is ongoing data collection and monitoring, credentialing verifies professional qualifications, and utilization review evaluates the appropriateness or necessity of services rather than peer performance comparison.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ Digital Healthcare Research — Benchmarking: benchmarking evaluates metrics and/or best practices from other organizations or reference standards and compares them with local performance to identify opportunities for improvement. Current AHRQ benchmarking workflow-assessment resource live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCLEX relevance independently verified against the 2026 NCSBN Management of Care performance-improvement activities. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A hospital compares its infection-rate performance with national or peer-organization data to identify opportunities for improvement. What is this process called?
